messages:
sana: Heads-up — p99 latency for tiny-seq (<=64 tokens) jumped from ~42ms -> ~120ms after yesterday's kernel32 change. Linking perf dump.
kevin: ugh, that's pretty bad. Is this across all models or just the quantized paths?
maria: quick look — seems concentrated on small-ctx requests that normally get coalesced into microbatches, they're spending more time in the queue.
jonathan: could be the combo of increased max_batch_tokens and a slower kernel handshake on the new build. what are current scheduler flags?
perf-bot: scheduler config snapshot: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=8, microbatch_target_tokens=256
kevin: 2048 is fairly large for tiny-seq. that effectively increases tolerance to wait for bigger batches.
sana: profiling numbers: queue_wait_ms median=15ms, p95=48ms, p99=92ms for seq<=64; dispatch and kernel exec times are stable. queueing looks like the culprit.
maria: simple mitigation: reduce effective max_batch_tokens for very short sequences or lower max_wait_ms for them.
jonathan: propose a two-tier policy: for seq_len<=64 use max_batch_tokens=512 and max_wait_ms=4; for others keep current.
kevin: can we do this per-shard so we can canary? don't want global impact before we confirm.
sana: yes — scheduler supports rule overrides per shard. i'll run a 5% canary. expected improvement: p99 down to ~40-55ms from simulation.
maria: note: KV cache-miss rate for tiny-seq spiked ~10% over baseline which causes extra kernel path (more work) and increases variance — we should track that too.
jonathan: good catch. kernel-selection telemetry would help us correlate misses -> fallback kernels -> tail. add counters for kernel_variant and kv_cache_hit.
sana: plan: (1) deploy per-seq heuristic to canary, (2) enable kernel-selection + kv telemetry, (3) capture p50/p95/p99 and queue histograms.
kevin: i'll open the rollout PR for the scheduler rule. will include canary-shard target and rollback window.
sana: config snippet i'll use in the PR:

```
policy:
  - name: tiny-seq
    condition: seq_len <= 64
    scheduler:
      max_batch_tokens: 512
      max_wait_ms: 4
```

sana: starting canary now and collecting 30m traces. will post results in ~40m.
maria: thanks — if p99 still >60ms after this tweak we should instrument kernel fallback frequency and consider a fast-path kernel for tiny sequences.
jonathan: also watch throughput and cost: smaller batching may reduce tokens/sec efficiency. acceptable trade if SLOs recover.
perf-bot: canary started: shard=canary-3, traffic=5%, start_ts=1981234567
kevin: ping me when traces posted, i'll help analyze :thumbsup:
